title: I wanted to build something where anyone can experience any life. 3 months in, here's one scene and where I'm stuck.
author: worldcv
selftext:
I started building this because I wanted to create a platform that allows anyone to experience any life. Pick someone from history, or make someone up, and play one day of theirs. Nothing is written ahead of time. The scenes get written as you reach them, the room and the people get painted the first time anyone opens that day, and the lines are read out loud.

The video is one scene off the live site, real speed, cut for length. Titanic wireless room, April 14 1912.

Stack: Opus 5 writes the scenes and the day plan. Gemini 3.7 Flash does the cheap stuff, minting the character, the day's first sketch, reading whatever you type. Gemini for images and voice, ElevenLabs forced alignment for lip sync. Each room gets painted once and each person rendered once, so the second person to open a day pays for zero images. A fresh day costs me $1 to $2, mostly images.

Im still unsure of the angle here: live any layman life? any extraordinary life? real lives? im still trying to figure this out. Also visual fidelity, is 2d enough? should it bubble up to spatial 3d eventually?

First day is free, no account: [https://sonder.gg/united-kingdom/1912/frank-garside?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=aigamedev&utm\_campaign=2026-09-14-one-scene](https://sonder.gg/united-kingdom/1912/frank-garside?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=aigamedev&utm_campaign=2026-09-14-one-scene)
